items.text: – You did the best thing, Nini-jan. They say newborns need a lot of sleep. Ten hours a day.
items.q: Amir lovingly calls his mother 'Nini', an endearment used in the family. Does it sound warm and natural?
before: – Amir-jan, while you were all exchanging Norouz greetings with the children, I grabbed a little nap.

items.q: Farid has just called Amir twice. Does 'Yeah, right' clearly mean 'obviously I was calling you'?
before: …bunk above mine, the bed that for three years had been a reminder of Bahman's absence. Farid had put on his jeans, but he still had not put on his socks. He had a habit of putting on his trousers, then going over to sit on the bed and eat breakfast. With his mouth full, he called me again. I said:

items.text: – Oh-ho. Hamid Cat, until yesterday you said "ass." Now you've gone all civilized and say "donkey"?
items.q: Taghi mocks Hamid for swapping a rude word for a polite one. Does it land?
before: – Pfff, donkey, who knows better, the friend of the cousin of our brother-in-law's master craftsman who is the richest man in Tehran, or you, you calf? Go on then, buy it. But when its glass breaks, don't say I didn't warn you.

items.text: In a way, you could say they conquered the university. Karroubi is love, honestly and truly.
items.q: Farid is excited. Does 'Karroubi is love' sound like natural student slang?
before: – Hey, Taverny, run! Come on, let's go. They say they didn't let Karroubi into the university. His supporters broke the Hafez gate and came in.

items.text: I press the elevator button. The elevator door opens. That day, Niloofar had come up the stairs. I go toward the stairwell. The voices of a boy and a girl drift out of the elevator. They call me sick.
items.q: The riders mock him for calling the elevator, then walking off. Does 'sick' land?

items.text: – And with that dickish way you talk, your name should've been Alain Dickon. Don't flatter yourself. I don't mean Alain Delon, with the way you scrunch up your nose ...
items.q: Hooman's insult puns on the actor Alain Delon. Does 'Alain Dickon' land?

items.text: – In my opinion, life is like a thousand-toman banknote: whichever side you look at, it smells of lentil rice.
items.q: Meysam ends a deep debate about life with a silly quip. Does the joke land?
before: Meysam and Eskandar sat there in the dark, debating. The conversation had reached the meaning of life and was beginning to sound like an argument. Eskandar's voice kept rising until Meysam said:

items.text: After that, like a screw with stripped threads, that image was no longer bound to the darkness behind the closed door of our house.
items.q: The memory came loose from that one place. Is the screw image clear?
before: …as memories passing through the mind, but as though I have been hurled back into that very moment, that very place. Several more times I found myself trapped behind the same door, within the same mingling of light and darkness. Each time, the same images passed before my eyes, damp and unsettling.

items.text: – It's marmal stone. Marmal means really expensive.
items.q: Both mistakes are intended: little Ghassem says 'marmal' for marble and thinks it means expensive. Does it sound like a child?
before: We went on again. There was a house halfway there. Its wall was pretty. Ghassem always said:

items.text: – Yeah, I've heard a few things about this localization business.
items.q: Eskandar means the regional quota system for university places. Is 'localization' clear for that?

items.text: He can't help it. That's just his factory setting. Always so elegant and formal, shitting right at the historic turning point.
items.q: Hooman mocks Amir for messing up at a key moment. Does this read naturally?

items.text: – Kids, we've been watching a movie at our relatives' house.
items.q: A schoolboy addresses his friends. Does 'Kids' sound natural from him?

items.text: With that toy car he pulled along behind him, he would surely fall from Negar's eyes.
items.q: The boys all want to impress Negar. Is the meaning of the Persian idiom 'fall from Negar's eyes' clear?
before: …A few days later, Taghi came to our usual spot with his toy car. Since Negar had entered our childish world, we had forgotten playing with cars. Not only playing with cars; all games had gone into the house of forgetting. I was very happy. With his own hands, Taghi was pinning himself to the mat.

items.text: That Dr. Shafiʿi Kadkani had taken my poem and said he'd read it later? Just a harvest-time promise?
items.q: This is a Persian saying kept literal. Is the meaning of 'a harvest-time promise' clear here?

items.text: It makes you shit-dizzy. The more you think about it, the more shit-dizzy you get.
items.q: A student's crude made-up word for baffling. Does 'shit-dizzy' work as slang?
before: – ... Look at it, it's genuinely mind-bending. He drew this and wrote underneath it: this is not a pipe.

items.text: They dumped earth over her with a buldozel. Earth and lime.
items.q: Maman says 'buldozel' for bulldozer on purpose. Does it read as her slip, not a typo?
